Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
8:43 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying faster, cheaper and easier than cash or cards. You scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. It works at a tea stall as easily as at a big store, and it runs all day, every day, including holidays.

It also helped that the system was built to be open. Any bank or payment app can join it, so you are not locked into one company. Shopkeepers needed no special machine, just a printed QR code, which let even the smallest sellers accept digital payments.

Three main reasons:

Free and instant: Most payments between people and at shops cost nothing, and the money arrives right away.
Works for everyone: One QR code or phone number works across apps and banks, with no card machine needed.
Simple and trusted: A PIN on your own phone, a record of every payment, and the backing of the banking system make it feel safe.

Together, these made UPI the default way to pay for millions of people, from big cities to small towns.
